A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Olbedo, with the same dataset and core pipeline. All 16 pages of each version, including the complete supplements, support reliable comparison of text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning results on MatrixCity in Table 1 and qualitative relighting, segmentation, material-editing and change-detection experiments in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds evaluated methods, NIID-Net fine-tuning results, prediction-error maps and examples of label-generation failures.

M1.justification: The sun–sky decomposition, geometry/shadow confidence masks and diffusion-model LoRA procedure are retained. Normalization and overcast handling are newly documented without establishing a revised underlying algorithm. NIID-Net is an additional evaluated baseline using its original architecture and training pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 5,664-image Olbedo corpus, MatrixCity benchmark, BlendedMVS and self-collected UAV scenes, and parking-lot application data. The tasks remain unchanged. The disclosed clean subset and additional diagnostic examples do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4 and Table 1 expand the comparison from three diffusion methods to six methods by adding Colorful Diffuse, IntrinsicAnything and NIID-Net. NIID-Net is evaluated before and after fine-tuning; the other two additions use pretrained checkpoints. This substantially broadens comparison across architectures and training approaches.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce native NIID-Net fine-tuning and pretrained-only evaluation for Colorful Diffuse and IntrinsicAnything. The existing 520-image MatrixCity test, resizing, unaligned metrics and diffusion fine-tuning settings remain unchanged. v2 still specifies full-dataset training, so the screened subset does not establish a changed training sample count.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds spatial error-map analysis, and Appendix C adds qualitative diagnostics for geometry holes, shadow-boundary noise, tree geometry, glass reflection and transmission. These are focused additions to error analysis. Most application examples are retained or relocated, although one material-editing case is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The binary confidence masks concern supervision validity, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds results for IntrinsicAnything, Colorful Diffuse and NIID-Net, extending the empirical evidence beyond diffusion-only fine-tuning. NIID-Net improves from 12.782/0.549/0.793 to 16.152/0.594/0.769 in PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS. The six original rows and RGB↔X's overall lead are unchanged. New error/failure visualizations are reported, while the dark-gray recoloring example from v1 supplementary Figure 8 is omitted.

T1.justification: Main-text Equations (1)–(3) and the supplementary rendering and sun–sky derivations retain their mathematical content. Appendix equations are renumbered, and the diffuse-surface assumptions receive clearer discussion, without new formal assumptions, proofs or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the claimed fine-tuning benefit from diffusion models to both CNN and diffusion architectures. The introduction also qualifies Olbedo's labels as pseudo-ground-truth. The central dataset contribution, complementarity with synthetic pretraining and downstream application claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands qualification of label reliability and applicability: it discusses reflectance-model violations, insufficient shadow pairs under overcast skies, limited scene diversity and site imbalance. It narrows the interpretation of confidence masks to geometry/shadow boundaries and explains why evaluation against in-domain pseudo-labels could overstate accuracy.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents 98th-percentile albedo normalization, sky-only overcast handling, approximately 3 cm reconstruction accuracy and a manually screened 2.49k-image subset, whose training use remains unspecified. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit grayscale differencing, threshold of 30 and morphological postprocessing instructions for change detection.

R1.justification: Colorful Diffuse and NIID-Net are newly cited and incorporated into the positioning across model families. DeepLabv3, Mask R-CNN and LAION-5B citations disappear with shortened discussion. The related-work taxonomy and central gap concerning real outdoor aerial supervision remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The applications section is extensively condensed from four numbered subsections into short paragraphs, while the evaluation narrative is expanded and rewritten. The supplement is reorganized around a new failure-case section, with separate editing/change-analysis sections removed as examples move into the main text. Terminology and affiliation details also change.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is redesigned to include additional methods and error maps, Table 1 expands, and Figure C.1 introduces failure examples. Application panels are consolidated between the main text and supplement, the confidence-mask display is enlarged, and duplicate segmentation content is cropped. These substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The additional CNN transfer experiment and explicit pseudo-label failure analysis strengthen evidence for Olbedo's usefulness and clarify its limitations. These gains outweigh the removal of change-detection implementation details and one editing example. The improvement is limited: the underlying dataset, evaluation coverage and original benchmark results remain unchanged.
